title: Standard Returns and Refunds Policy
section: 1 · Eligibility window and what the customer may request
text:
[Doc: C1RETURNSREFEXCH-D1 | Category: Returns & Exchanges | Title: Standard Returns and Refunds Policy]
An eligible change-of-mind return may be raised within 30 calendar days of the recorded delivery date. The window is

calculated from the carrier “delivered” event captured in the approved order record, not from the order date or the

invoice date.

Within the 30-day window the customer may request (a) a refund to the original payment method, (b) a same-order

exchange for an identical SKU at a different size or colour, or (c) a Northstar store-credit code (NSC-SC- prefix,

36-month validity). A partial refund against a single multi-item order is processed under form code RET-30-PR; the

remaining items stay on the original order.

Outside the 30-day window the request must be reclassified against C1RR-D13 (Late returns and policy-window

exceptions) and may not be approved under this document. Items reported damaged in transit, dead-on-arrival or

incorrect are routed to C1RR-D3, not here.

initiation timer.

If inspection passes, the refund is initiated within 5 working days of the inspection timestamp being written to the

approved system. The customer’s card or payment provider may then take a further 3–5 working days to post the

evidence are present. A draft must not say “refund sent” from approval alone, and must not promise a calendar-day

deadline.

section: 1 · How the prepaid label is generated
text:
[Doc: C1RETURNSREFEXCH-D10 | Category: Returns & Exchanges | Title: Return Shipping Labels, Prepaid QR Codes and Drop-off]
The customer opens portal route /returns/label in a browser and enters the order reference plus the RMA reason code.

The portal returns a QR-coded label as a PDF and an RMA reference of the form RMA-RPD-, RMA-EVRI- or

RMA-DPD- depending on the selected carrier scheme.

The label is free of charge for change-of-mind returns when the original order value was £75 or more. For orders below

the £75 threshold the label carries a £3.95 deduction from the refund (label fee code RPD-FEE-3.95). The fee is

always waived for C1RR-D3 (damaged, defective, DOA) and C1RR-D6 (gift) returns.

text:
[Doc: C1RETURNSREFEXCH-D10 | Category: Returns & Exchanges | Title: Return Shipping Labels, Prepaid QR Codes and Drop-off]
The prepaid QR code can be scanned at any UK ParcelShop in the three carrier networks. The drop-off list is at portal

route /returns/drop-off and is filtered by postcode. Coverage includes convenience stores, newsagents and a small

number of supermarket collection points; the network list is updated weekly.

Scan-in at the ParcelShop creates a carrier event in the approved system with the carrier’s tracking number and the

ParcelShop identifier (PS-XXXX format). The customer’s draft status moves from “approved—not sent” to “in transit”

and then to “received at hub” once the carrier event is recorded at the Returns Hub.

A missing-item case is opened by the Returns Hub when the inspection record shows fewer SKUs than the original

human approval.

section: 1 · When a direct exchange is allowed
text:
[Doc: C1RETURNSREFEXCH-D12 | Category: Returns & Exchanges | Title: Size and Variant Direct Exchange Procedure]
A direct exchange is allowed only for a size or colour swap within the same SKU family. The original item must be

eligible under C1RR-D1 (within the 30-day window), the new variant must be in stock at the recorded warehouse, and

the customer must agree to the exchange before the original item is collected.

Only one exchange is allowed per order reference. A second exchange attempt on the same order is refused and the

customer is asked to use the standard refund route and place a new order if they still want a different variant.

text:
[Doc: C1RETURNSREFEXCH-D14 | Category: Returns & Exchanges | Title: Refund Processing Timelines and Original Payment Reversal]
“Refund initiated” means the refund record has been written to the approved payments system. It does not mean the

customer’s bank or card statement has been updated. The customer-facing draft must use the word “initiated” rather

than “sent” or “received”.

Card refunds (Visa / Mastercard / Amex) typically appear on the customer’s statement within 3–5 working days of

initiation; PayPal refunds are usually visible in 1–3 working days; Apple Pay follows the underlying card. Klarna and

Clearpay reversals may take up to 7 working days because the BNPL provider has to unwind any instalments already

scheduled.

title: Refund Processing Timelines and Original Payment Reversal
section: 2 · Partial refunds, multi-tender splits and rounding
text:
[Doc: C1RETURNSREFEXCH-D14 | Category: Returns & Exchanges | Title: Refund Processing Timelines and Original Payment Reversal]
Partial refunds (form code PAY-PART) are initiated against the same tender used for the original charge. Where an

order was paid with a multi-tender split (form code PAY-MULTI) — for example, £40.00 on card and £10.00 in store

credit — the refund is split proportionally across the tenders, not applied to one tender alone.

Refunds are rounded to the smallest currency unit (pence). Multi-tender splits are calculated in pence first and then

presented as pounds and pence, so the sum of the tender refunds equals the total refund to the penny. Rounding

errors are never absorbed silently — they are surfaced to the human approver before initiation.

title: Return Abuse, Serial Wardrobing and Account Flags
section: 1 · What counts as a return-abuse pattern
text:
[Doc: C1RETURNSREFEXCH-D15 | Category: Returns & Exchanges | Title: Return Abuse, Serial Wardrobing and Account Flags]
A return-abuse pattern is a sequence of returns that is consistent with using the return policy as a try-on or

try-before-you-buy service rather than as genuine change-of-mind or fault handling. The pilot triggers are mechanical

and based on the approved order record.

FLG-R01 is set when the customer completes four returns in any rolling 90-day window. FLG-R02 is set when the

items returned show clear signs of use beyond what is needed to evaluate fit (wardrobing — e.g. removed tags,

makeup marks, fragrance). FLG-R03 is set when a high proportion of returns arrive within 48 hours of an event

recorded on the customer’s calendar (post-event return). FLG-R04 is set when the same delivery address or payment

method is shared across more than one account with high return rates. FLG-R05 is set when the returned items are

suspected of being intended for resale.

section: 2 · What the flags do and what they do not do
text:
[Doc: C1RETURNSREFEXCH-D15 | Category: Returns & Exchanges | Title: Return Abuse, Serial Wardrobing and Account Flags]
A flag is an internal marker on the customer record. It does not, by itself, refuse a return. A human reviewer reads the

flag, the pattern that produced it and the most recent return request, and decides whether the next return is handled

under the standard route or under a manager-approved variant (for example, store-credit-only under C1RR-D6 instead

of refund-to-card).

A flag is not shared with the customer unless the human reviewer decides that a brief, neutral explanation is

appropriate. The customer is never told the literal flag code (FLG-R01 etc.) and the wording must not be accusatory.

[Doc: C1RETURNSREFEXCH-D2 | Category: Returns & Exchanges | Title: Holiday and Seasonal Extended Returns]
Orders placed during a Northstar Supplies Ltd. promotional trade period and carrying a HOL- SKU prefix or a recorded

campaign code from the set {BF-2026, XM-2026, NY-2026} qualify for an extended return window. The base 30

calendar-day window defined in C1RR-D1 is extended to 60 calendar days from delivery.

For Black Friday 2026 (BF-2026) the window is 60 calendar days from delivery for items delivered between 1

November 2026 and 24 December 2026 inclusive. For Christmas / New Year (XM-2026, NY-2026) the window is 60

calendar days from delivery for items delivered between 25 December 2026 and 14 February 2027 inclusive. Outside

those delivery bands the base window applies.

The extension does not apply to non-holiday catalogue items, to items purchased in the same basket but without a

HOL- prefix, or to items already excluded under C1RR-D4 (final sale, clearance and non-returnable items).

resealed packaging) that is consistent with carrier handling. The carrier event is logged against form code RET-DMG

and an INC-ARR carrier incident is opened in parallel.

description states, and the customer has not used it beyond a single power-on attempt. Logged under form code

caused by misuse, incompatible accessories or environmental factors outside the catalogue specification. Logged

under form code RET-DEF. After 7 calendar days the request routes to C1RR-D8-style warranty handling (NS-WAR).

A gift return is raised by someone who is not the original buyer. The original payment method is not on file in the same

order. A human approver confirms the unwind but does not invent a different basis; the recorded prices are the only

source of truth.

refund is the full amount paid for that item (because nothing was paid for it). If the paid item is returned, the refund is

the amount paid minus the standard non-promotional unit price of the kept item. Form code RET-BOGO.

free gift is also returned, the free gift is simply not refunded. If the qualifying purchase is returned but the free gift is

kept, the value of the free gift (FG- price code) is deducted from the refund. Form code RET-FG.

reason is C1RR-D3 (damaged, defective, DOA) or NS-WAR (warranty). The reimbursement is capped at £25.00 per

parcel for EU destinations and £45.00 per parcel for the rest of the in-scope set.

title: International Returns, Customs and Duties Recovery
text:
[Doc: C1RETURNSREFEXCH-D9 | Category: Returns & Exchanges | Title: International Returns, Customs and Duties Recovery]
Every international return parcel must carry a customs declaration. For parcels under £270 in declared value, the CN22

form is used; for parcels at £270 or above, the CN23 form is required. The reason for return is written as “Returned

goods — Northstar Supplies Ltd. order ”. The HS tariff code for the original SKU is reused from the outbound shipment

record.

If the original outbound shipment was sent Delivered Duty Paid (DDP), Northstar may be able to recover the original

duties from the destination customs authority. A duty-recovery request is logged as form code DDP-RECV and is

processed by the International Logistics team within 30 working days of the return being received. The recovery, if any,

is passed on to the customer as an additional refund under the original payment method; recovery is not guaranteed.
